title: Per-route quality contract and deferred traffic reallocation procedure
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Define a per-route Service Quality Contract (SQC) that pairs concrete SLI measurements with automated deferred traffic reallocation rules. Goal: standardize how we define per-endpoint/model SLOs for different traffic tiers, automate progressive mitigation (from throttling to model-variant fallback to cross-region reallocation), and codify circuit breaker thresholds so on-call & autoscale can take deterministic actions during sustained error-budget burn.
background_and_rationale: Recent incidents (INC-2025-147: multi-region spike during model rollout) revealed inconsistent SLI definitions across routes and opaque decisions for failover. Different teams configured brittle circuit breakers and manual migration steps. We need a single operational contract per route that is machine-readable, backed by dashboards, and exercised by automated runbooks. This improves predictability for customers and reduces manual toil for SREs.
sli_definitions: Availability SLI: fraction of successful HTTP 200-like responses that pass model-quality checks (response.status in 2xx AND quality_score >= 0.80) over 30m windows
Latency SLI: tail latencies measured per-request (first-byte and end-to-end) exposed as p50/p95/p99 — grouped by route-class
Quality SLI: automated quality regression score computed by yearly prompt-set evals and online sampling (avg quality_score over 24h), per model variant and per route
Error SLI: ratio of requests returning 5xx or timeouts to total requests in 1h windows
Throughput SLI: tokens/sec served per route vs. capacity target (for capacity-aware SLOs)
slo_targets_by_route_class: Tier: interactive-chat — Availability >= 99.5% (30d), p95 first-byte latency <= 250ms, quality_score >= 0.85
Tier: high-throughput-embedding — Availability >= 99.9% (30d), p95 latency <= 120ms, quality_score >= 0.90
Tier: batch-rerank — Availability >= 99.0% (30d), p95 latency <= 2000ms, quality_score >= 0.80
error_budget_policy: Compute error budget as 100% - Availability target over rolling 30d window
Burn rules: sustained burn rate > 2x over 6h -> notify SRE and pause non-critical canaries
- Level 1 (10% budget burned in period): enable increased tracing and throttle 5% of low-priority traffic
- Level 2 (40% burned): route low-priority traffic to cached/quantized variants; enable regional spill-to-secondary policy
- Level 3 (80% burned): trigger circuit breaker for non-SLA routes, initiate cross-region failover window and on-call page
Budget credits and reclamation: successful mitigations return credit if full functionality is restored within 24h
multi_region_failover_policy: Failover priority matrix: local-readiness -> regional-primary -> regional-secondary -> global-fallback
Reroute window: progressively reallocate up to 30% of traffic to secondary region within first 5 minutes; 70% by 30 minutes if metrics degrade further
Latency-aware routing: prefer regions where p95 latency to first byte < route SLO and quality_score delta < 0.03
Stateful sessions: prefer sticky routing where KV cache available; otherwise prefer warm model-variant with prefilled KV cache
Manual override: product-owners can pin routes to region via Console with immediate effect (audited)
circuit_breaker_spec: Open conditions (per 1m sliding window): error_rate >= 5% AND p99 latency > 3x SLO
Half-open probe: allow 5% of requests to test restored capacity for 60s before full close
Per-route queue thresholds: queue length > 500 -> shed lowest priority requests or downgrade to quantized variant
Variant-aware breakers: if a model-variant triggers >3 consecutive opens, mark variant as degraded and shift traffic away until manual review
load_shedding_algorithm: Priority-based: each request gets a priority score (customer_tier, route_criticality, request_length, cached_hit) — lower priority requests shed first
Token-length aware: for expensive long-sequence requests, probabilistic admission to keep tail latency bounded
Graceful degradation steps: 1) use cached prefixes/KV responses; 2) downgrade to quantized model variant; 3) truncate generation length; 4) return 429 with Retry-After when all else exhausted
Client signals: honor client-declared importance headers (X-Redwood-Priority) but cap for fairness across tenants
metrics_and_dashboards: Dashboard: SQC Summary — per-route availability, burn rate, quality_score, active mitigations (link below)
Alerting: Pager at >80% burn in 24h; Pager at >50% with rising trend and p95 > SLO for 2 consecutive 1h windows
Sampling: 0.5% production sampling for automated quality scoring and human review pipeline
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 wks): define canonical SQC JSON schema, add SLI collectors for quality_score and first-byte latency
Phase 2 (3 wks): implement automated error-budget monitor and simple mitigation actions (throttle low-priority) behind feature flag
Phase 3 (4 wks): integrate region reallocation and circuit breaker engine; add Console controls for pinning/fallback
Phase 4 (2 wks): rollout to beta routes, validate against canaries, and run tabletop exercise with SREs and PMs
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable SQC schema exists and is stored in config-store with versioning
SLI collectors show consistent metrics for at least 3 production routes across 7 days
Automated mitigations can be toggled and observed in dashboard with end-to-end audit logs
Failover path exercised in a non-prod region and verified by SRE team checklist
Belonging product teams have signed off on per-route contracts for beta routes

risks_and_open_questions: Risk: quality_score tooling may not correlate with human judgment for niche prompt sets — mitigation: human review sampling
Question: should we expose per-customer configurable SLOs or keep global per-route tiers? (trade-off: complexity vs customer SLAs)
Risk: cross-region KV cache warmup cost could spike during failover — mitigation: pre-warm policy and conservative initial reallocation percentage
Question: how to account for token-cost when downgrading to quantized variants (cost vs. quality trade-off)
